questions.prompt: What tells an agent that a junto call failed?

choices.why: Messages are written for people and can change; code should not parse them.

choices.text: ok: false and a typed error
choices.why: Every failure prints ok: false with an error whose type names the kind of failure, on stderr with exit code 1.
A failure has no data field at all; it carries error instead.

choices.text: A line that is not JSON
choices.why: The CLI prints one JSON envelope for success and failure alike.

questions.prompt: Can an agent act as another seat by naming that seat in a call?

choices.text: Yes, by passing its id as the target
choices.why: A target names who you call, never who you are.

choices.text: Yes, if both seats share a region
choices.why: Sharing a region makes a seat visible; it never changes who the caller is.

choices.text: No: identity comes from the credential in its own environment
choices.why: Junto mints JUNTO_WORK_TOKEN for each seat process; the CLI presents it, and a process without it is refused.

questions.prompt: A call fails with Paused and retryable: true. What should the agent do?

choices.text: Retry in a loop until it passes
choices.why: Retries are bounded: at most twice, then adapt or escalate.

choices.text: Wait for the operator to play the canvas, and retry at most twice
choices.why: A paused canvas refuses writes until play, and the retry law allows at most two retries.
Paused is not a problem the operator must solve for this seat; waiting is the first move.
retryable: true says a later attempt may pass.
